Operator: Good day, and welcome to the SecureNet Solutions Q2 FY24 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during this time, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SecureNet Solutions' results for the Q2 FY24. With me on today's call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Technology Officer, and Raj Singh, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. SecureNet Solutions had an exceptional Q2, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers.

Our strategy is centered around five core pillars: expanding our number of customers with ARR over $100K, increasing average deal sizes for new and existing customers, mitigating the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue, sustaining robust R&D investment as a percentage of revenue, and accelerating the number of new customers acquired.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah highlighted, we had a remarkable Q2. Revenue reached $712 million, reflecting a 28% year-over-year increase. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 78%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $480 million, and net income was $112 million, translating to $0.85 per diluted share. We are increasing our guidance for the full year to $2.95-3.0 billion in revenue, implying 27-29% growth at the midpoint.

Let me dive deeper into the metrics that underscore our momentum in the cybersecurity landscape. First, on our number of customers with annual recurring revenue, or ARR, exceeding $100K. This group is a cornerstone of our land-and-expand strategy, reflecting deep penetration into Fortune 1000 enterprises and large-scale deployments where our XDR platform, SecureNet Sentinel, delivers mission-critical threat detection, response, and zero-trust enforcement.

In Q2, we ended the quarter with 528 customers generating over $100K in ARR—that's a robust 17% quarter-over-quarter increase from 451 in Q1 FY24, and a stellar 32% year-over-year growth from 400 in Q2 FY23. For context, these high-value customers now represent just 10.5% of our total customer base of approximately 5,000, but they account for 68% of our total ARR—up from 64% a year ago. This concentration speaks to our maturing go-to-market motion, where we're not just winning logos but driving multi-year, multi-product expansions.

Breaking this down by key trends and drivers, net revenue retention, or NRR, within this segment hit 128% in Q2, fueled by existing customers expanding their footprint. Average ARR per customer in this group grew 12% year-over-year to $245K, driven by upsells into our AI-powered modules like Sentinel Threat Intelligence and our Cloud Workload Protection Platform, or CWPP, which integrates seamlessly with hyperscalers such as AWS and Azure. We've seen particular strength in bundled offerings combining our Endpoint Detection and Response, or EDR, with Secure Access Service Edge, or SASE, capabilities, addressing the post-SolarWinds and Log4j era of supply chain vulnerabilities.

Regionally, North America continues to dominate, comprising 72% of this cohort with 380 customers—up 22% year-over-year—as enterprises like those in financial services and healthcare double down amid surging ransomware incidents, reminiscent of the Change Healthcare breach earlier this year. Our EMEA business accelerated to 95 customers, a 48% year-over-year surge, propelled by NIS2 Directive compliance deadlines and GDPR enforcement, where we've displaced legacy players like Symantec in several key wins. APAC, now at 53 customers—up 38% year-over-year—is gaining traction with data sovereignty mandates in markets like Singapore and Australia; we've secured partnerships with telcos like Singtel to embed our Zero Trust Network Access, or ZTNA, into their 5G ecosystems.

On the technical front, our initiatives are yielding tangible results. The rollout of GenAI-accelerated anomaly detection in Sentinel—which reduced mean time to detect, or MTTD, by 40% in beta trials—has been a game-changer for expansions. Customers like a top-tier U.S. bank expanded from $150K to $450K ARR by layering our Extended Detection and Response, or XDR, over their existing Splunk SIEM stack. Similarly, our converged SASE/XDR platform has resonated in manufacturing, where we've added 15 new $100K+ logos amid rising OT/IoT threats from nation-state actors.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on three pillars to sustain this trajectory: one, enterprise-grade scalability—we've invested in FedRAMP High authorization, unlocking U.S. federal opportunities and positioning us against incumbents like Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud. Two, channel acceleration—our partner ecosystem, including MSSPs like Accenture and Deloitte, contributed 35% of new $100K+ wins, with co-sell motions around our MITRE ATT&CK-aligned coverage. Three, AI moat expansion—with R&D spend up 25% year-over-year, we're outpacing the industry average in generative AI for threat hunting, targeting a NRR north of 130% by FY25 end.

Looking ahead, we expect this metric to grow 25-30% year-over-year in FY24, supported by a $2.1B pipeline where 60% is from existing customers. This isn't just growth; it's sticky, high-margin revenue in a market projected by Gartner to exceed $200B by 2027, amid persistent macro tailwinds like geopolitical tensions and regulatory pressures.

Shifting to another key performance indicator: average deal size, or ADS, segmented by new and existing customers. In the cybersecurity SaaS landscape, ADS is a critical leading indicator of our go-to-market execution, customer value realization, and overall revenue quality. We measure this primarily on an Annual Contract Value, or ACV, basis to reflect the recurring revenue momentum from our platform—think of it as the annualized value of new bookings from our core offerings like our Next-Gen Endpoint Detection and Response, or EDR, Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform, or CNAPP, and Secure Access Service Edge, or SASE, stack.

For Q2, average deal size for new customers came in at $285,000 ACV, up 22% year-over-year from $234,000 in Q2 2023. This marks our 8th consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year expansion for new logos, driven by a deliberate shift toward enterprise-scale deployments. New customer deals now average 3.2 modules per contract—up from 2.1 a year ago—with strong uptake in our AI-powered XDR module, which bundles EDR, network detection, and deception tech into a unified platform. We're seeing this in wins like our recent hyperscaler partnership expansion, mirroring trends at peers like CrowdStrike with Falcon Flex and Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud, where customers consolidate point solutions amid escalating ransomware threats—up 35% in incidents per our Q2 Threat Report.

On the existing customer side, average deal size hit $162,000 ACV, a healthy 18% year-over-year increase from $137,000. This reflects our land-and-expand model in action, with dollar-based net retention holding steady at 128%—well above the industry average of 115-120% for public cyber peers. Expansions are fueled by 65% of Q2 renewals adding at least one net-new module, particularly our ZTNA and Cloud Workload Protection, or CWP, capabilities. For context, 42% of these upsells came from customers scaling to our Autonomous SOC offering, which leverages generative AI for automated threat hunting and response—reducing mean time to respond, or MTTR, by 60% in beta deployments. This mirrors Zscaler's SASE momentum and SentinelOne's Singularity platform expansions, as enterprises grapple with hybrid work and multi-cloud sprawl.

Trend-wise, the divergence between new and existing ADS is narrowing, now at just 76% of new-logo size versus 110% last year. This convergence signals maturing platform stickiness: our net promoter score, or NPS, for multi-module customers sits at 72, versus 58 for single-product users. We've also seen a 15% quarter-over-quarter lift in total contract value, or TCV, multiples, averaging 2.8x ACV, as customers opt for 3-year commitments amid economic uncertainty—locking in pricing ahead of our anticipated 8-10% guide for FY25 price optimization.

Regionally, performance is differentiated but positive. In the Americas, which represent 62% of Q2 bookings, new customer ADS led at $312,000, buoyed by Fortune 1000 wins in financial services and healthcare—sectors hit hardest by Log4j-style vulnerabilities and Magecart attacks. EMEA clocked in at $265,000 for new deals, up 28% year-over-year, thanks to GDPR-driven compliance mandates and our new Paris data region, accelerating deals with telcos like those partnering with Netskope. APAC/Japan, now 18% of bookings, showed the fastest growth at $240,000 new ADS—31% year-over-year—propelled by sovereign cloud initiatives in Australia and Japan's MIC cybersecurity framework; however, existing ADS here lags at $138,000 due to longer sales cycles in regulated industries.

Strategically, these trends underscore our focus on platformization and outcome-based selling. We've invested heavily in co-engineered proofs-of-concept, or POCs, with integrations to Splunk, ServiceNow, and AWS Security Hub, shortening sales cycles by 25% to 90 days for deals over $500K ACV. Looking ahead, our Q3 pipeline—up 35% year-over-year in dollar terms—suggests new customer ADS will sustain 20%+ growth, with existing expansions benefiting from our Q3 launch of Agentless Cloud Security for serverless workloads. This positions us to outpace the 15% cyber market growth projected by Gartner for 2024, even as macro headwinds like high interest rates pressure SMB segments.

Before moving on, a note on the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations on our revenue. As a global leader in cybersecurity with over 60% of our revenue derived from international markets, we're exposed to currency volatility. In Q2, a strengthening U.S. dollar created a headwind, but our constant currency metrics underscore the underlying strength.

On a reported basis, Q2 revenue grew 24% year-over-year, but at constant currency, growth was 27%, reflecting a roughly 2.6 percentage point FX headwind. This was driven primarily by the USD appreciating against major revenue currencies: the euro weakened by about 4%, the British pound by 3.8%, and the Japanese yen by 7% amid Bank of Japan policies and U.S. Fed actions.

Regionally, Americas—55% of revenue at $392 million—saw minimal FX impact, as most is USD-denominated, with 29% growth both reported and constant currency, fueled by hyperscaler deals in cloud-native security like integrations with AWS and Azure for our SASE platform. EMEA—30% of revenue at $214 million—bore much of the brunt with a notable FX drag equivalent to about 5.6% of regional revenue; Eurozone sales grew 18% reported versus 24% constant currency, but our platform deployments in financial services held firm amid ransomware threats to EU infrastructure. APAC—15% at $106 million—faced disproportionate JPY depreciation; Japan reported modest growth masking stronger constant currency expansion, with traction via NTT Data partnerships for managed detection and response.

Our ARR grew 26% reported or 29% constant currency, with Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO, up 32%. Currency volatility has been ongoing, but we're mitigating through hedging 65-75% of forecasted exposure, capturing gains that offset over half the headwind. We've shifted 85% of new deals to local currency pricing, introduced multi-currency billing, accelerated localization like our Tokyo PoP for sovereign cloud, and embedded FX modeling in our sales stack. For Q3, we expect neutral to slight positive FX. These efforts de-risk us amid $212 billion global cybersecurity spend projections.

Turning to our R&D investment as a percentage of revenue—a leading indicator of staying ahead in this landscape. In Q2, we invested $168 million in R&D, representing 24% of our total revenue. This marks a 200-basis-point expansion from 22% in Q2 FY2023 and a sequential uptick from 23% prior quarter.

Our R&D spend grew 28% year-over-year, outpacing revenue growth and aligning with leaders like CrowdStrike at 25-27%. For the first half, it's 23.5% of revenue. Focus is on AI-native threat detection (40% of budget), zero-trust orchestration (30%), and post-quantum resilience (20%). We've advanced generative AI in ShieldXDR for anomaly prediction, cutting MTTD dramatically; hardened CloudShield Gateway with micro-segmentation; and open-sourced Kyber encryption for NIST standards.

Geographically tailored: North America for CMMC compliance; APAC for ransomware defenses; EMEA for DORA/NIS2. This sustains 120% net retention, drives patents, and efficiencies via NVIDIA partnerships. We expect 23-25% in FY25 as revenue hits $3.2-3.4 billion.

Finally, on new customer acquisition, which highlights our platform-led strategy. In Q2, we added 452 new customers, a 36% year-over-year increase from 332, bringing total to over 5,400—outpacing industry 15-20% growth per IDC.

By segment: 128 enterprise wins (ACV >$250K, up 42%, avg $487K) with ShieldX Zero-Trust; 289 commercial/mid-market (up 39%, avg $112K) via channels and marketplaces; 35 SMB and 12 government. Regionally: 249 Americas (up 41%), 113 EMEA (48%), 90 APAC (22%).

Driven by product cadence like ShieldX 6.0 GenAI, channel scaling (52% pipeline), and vertical focus. Q3 expects 475-500 adds on $2.1B RPO.

Next, Dr. Patel will provide more technical details.

Dr. Lena Patel: Thank you, Mike. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape. We are investing heavily in research and development to stay ahead of the curve and deliver unparalleled value to our customers. Key areas of focus include advancing GenAI for threat hunting, zero-trust SASE convergence, quantum-resistant crypto, and autonomous SOC capabilities that integrate across EDR, XDR, CWPP, and ZTNA—reducing MTTD/MTTR dramatically while supporting multi-cloud and sovereign environments as highlighted in our metrics.

Raj Singh: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, with FedRAMP High, GDPR/NIS2 readiness, and MITRE ATT&CK coverage ensuring resilience against ransomware, supply chain attacks, and nation-state threats.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [pause] Thank you. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks for taking my question. Sarah or Mike, could you expand on the drivers behind the 32% year-over-year growth in $100K ARR customers, particularly in EMEA and APAC, and how that ties into your NRR outlook?

Sarah Chen: Thanks, John. Absolutely, the growth there stems from regulatory tailwinds like NIS2 and data sovereignty, plus our Sentinel platform's AI anomaly detection winning expansions. As Mike detailed, NRR at 128% with average ARR up 12% YoY positions us for 25-30% growth this year, backed by that strong pipeline.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Hi, great results. Mike, on average deal sizes, how sustainable is the convergence between new and existing ADS, and what role is the Autonomous SOC playing in upsells?

Mike Thompson: Hi Emily, thanks. The narrowing gap reflects platform stickiness—NPS 72 for multi-module users—and 65% of renewals adding modules. Autonomous SOC, with 60% MTTR reduction, drove 42% of upsells; with Q3 agentless launch, we see 20%+ ADS growth persisting.

Operator: Next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee: Thanks. Lena, with R&D at 24% of revenue, can you speak to the post-quantum initiatives and how they factor into federal wins?

Dr. Lena Patel: Sure, David. 20% of R&D targets quantum-resistant crypto; we've open-sourced Kyber library for NIST migration, critical post-MOVEit. This bolsters FedRAMP High and CMMC, growing federal ARR past $250M amid DoD priorities.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Rodriguez with Barclays.

Lisa Rodriguez: Congrats on the quarter. Mike or Sarah, given FX headwinds, how are new customer adds holding up internationally, and any Q3 color?

Sarah Chen: Thanks, Lisa. New adds were balanced—113 in EMEA up 48%, 90 APAC—with localization like Tokyo PoP mitigating FX. Hedging and local pricing captured gains; Q3 pipeline suggests 475-500 adds despite volatility.

Sarah Chen: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
